title: Afghan Bread (Naan-e Afghani, oval flatbread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar and add the water and oil to form a soft dough.
Knead for 8 to 10 minutes and let it rise covered for about 1 hour.
Divide into 4 portions, stretch each into a long oval about 1 cm thick and press lines lengthwise with your fingertips or a comb.
Sprinkle with nigella seeds and bake on a very hot tray or stone at 250 C for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and puffed, then serve warm.
Tear the bread into pieces to eat alongside curries, kebabs and soups.

title: Afghan Burger (Kabul street sandwich with chutney and fries)
steps: Mix the mince with the onion, garlic, coriander, cumin, pepper and salt and form 4 flat patties.
Fry or grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side until cooked through.
Warm the flatbreads on a griddle.
Spread chutney inside each bread, add the patty, cabbage, tomato and a handful of fries.
Fold or close and serve hot.

title: Afghan Salad (tomato, cucumber and mint salad)
steps: Put the tomatoes, cucumbers and onion in a large bowl.
Add the chillies and the chopped herbs.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper together and pour over the salad.
Toss gently, chill for 15 minutes and serve with kebabs or rice dishes.

title: Afghan Torshi (spiced vegetable pickle)
steps: Bring the vinegar, water, salt, sugar and turmeric to a boil and stir until dissolved.
Pack the vegetables, garlic and seeds into clean jars.
Pour the hot brine over the vegetables to cover them completely.
Cool, close the jars and refrigerate for at least 3 days before eating.
Keep refrigerated and serve as a sharp accompaniment to rice dishes and kebabs.

title: Aush (Afghan noodle and bean soup)

ingredients.name: kidney beans or chickpeas, drained (400 g)
spaghetti or thin wheat noodles, broken

steps: Fry the onion in the oil until golden, add half the garlic and the mince and cook until browned.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli flakes and salt, then add the water, beans and lentils and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Add the noodles and spinach and cook until the noodles are tender, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix the yoghurt with the remaining garlic and a pinch of salt.
Heat a little oil with the dried mint for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top with the garlic yoghurt and drizzle with the mint oil.

title: Aushak (Afghan leek dumplings with yoghurt and meat sauce)

ingredients.name: leeks or 2 bunches of scallions (green onions), finely chopped

steps: Mix the flour, salt and water into a firm dough, knead until smooth and rest it for 30 minutes.
Cook the chopped leeks in the oil with the chilli flakes and salt until soft and dry, then cool.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 8 cm squares or circles, fill each with a spoonful of leeks, fold over and press the edges firmly closed.
Brown the onion and mince in oil, add the tomato paste and water and simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Mix the yoghurt with the garlic and a pinch of salt.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 5 to 7 minutes until they float and the dough is tender, then drain.
Spread the garlic yoghurt on a plate, arrange the dumplings on top, spoon the meat sauce over and sprinkle with dried mint.

title: Gosh-e Feel (Afghan elephant-ear fried pastry)
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, cardamom and salt, then add the yoghurt, sugar and egg and knead to a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and rest it for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin and cut it into rectangles, pinch each at the centre to make a bow or ear shape, and press the edges closed.
Fry in medium-hot oil, turning once, until golden and crisp, and drain on paper.
Mix the icing sugar, pistachios and cardamom and dust it generously over the cooled pastries.

title: Kabuli Palaw (Afghan lamb rice with carrots and raisins)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or shanks, on the bone
long-grain basmati rice, washed and soaked 30 minutes
ground cumin seeds for the rice

steps: Fry the onions in half the oil until deep golden brown, add the lamb and brown it on all sides.
Add 3 cups of water or stock and the salt, cover and simmer for about 1 hour until the lamb is tender; drain, reserving the meat and 2 cups of the broth.
Boil the rice in plenty of salted water until just tender but still firm, then drain.
Return the lamb to the pot, spoon the rice over it, add 1 cup of the reserved broth and the cumin, then cover and steam on low heat for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile fry the carrot matchsticks in a little oil with the sugar until glazed and soft, then add the raisins and the spices and cook for 2 minutes more.
Mound the rice on a platter with the lamb on top or underneath, scatter the carrots, raisins and nuts over it and serve.

title: Koloocheh (Afghan Nowruz cookies)
steps: Heat the oven to 160 C and line a baking tray.
Beat the sugar, oil and egg yolks together until pale, then stir in the cardamom and rose water.
Mix in the flour, baking powder and salt to form a soft dough.
Roll into small balls, press a nut into the top of each and arrange them on the tray.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until set and lightly golden underneath, then cool on the tray.

title: Nargesi Kebab (Afghan egg-in-meat kebab)
steps: Knead the mince with the onion, garlic, spices, salt, breadcrumbs and raw egg until sticky and smooth.
Divide into 4 portions and flatten each in your palm.
Place a boiled egg in the centre of each portion and wrap the meat completely around it, sealing well.
Heat a little oil in a pan and brown the kebabs on all sides, then cover and cook gently for 10 to 12 minutes (or bake at 180 C for 25 minutes).
Rest for 5 minutes, slice in half to reveal the egg and serve with naan and chutney.

title: Shir Berenj (Afghan creamy rice and milk pudding)
steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it in 1 cup of water for 10 minutes until it has absorbed most of the water.
Add the milk and salt and cook over low heat for about 30 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is very soft and the mixture creamy.
Stir in the sugar and cardamom and cook for 5 more minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in the rose water and pour into small bowls.
Chill and top with crushed nuts before serving.

title: Shorba (Afghan lamb and vegetable soup)

ingredients.name: fresh coriander or mint to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a pot and brown the lamb with the onion until golden.
Add the turmeric, coriander, pepper and salt and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 1 hour until the lamb is almost tender.
Add the potatoes, carrots, tomatoes and chickpeas and cook for 25 to 30 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Serve hot with fresh herbs and naan.
